messages:
maria: FYI escalated from ACME — after last night's rollout their invoice-summary prompt returns very different phrasing, sometimes drops line items. attaching repro.
chris: can you paste the exact API call and model name? any change in tokenization noted?
maria: customer gave this minimal repro: 
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-open-7b-v2","input":"Summarize invoice:\n- Item A: $10\n- Item B: $20\nPlease include total."}'
```
They used to get: "Total: $30" but now sometimes reply: "Total: 30" (no dollar sign) and occasionally drops Item B line. They say it started after the chat-template pr we rolled last night.
zach: that's likely the chat template normalization that introduced a leading/trailing whitespace normalization and a subtle tokenizer subtoken shift. Not sure why it'd drop lines though.
maria: customer also attached before/after outputs — they match if we strip tokens differently. sharing snippet:
```
# before (2026-02-12):
Summarize invoice:
- Item A: $10
- Item B: $20
Total: $30

# after (post-deploy):
Summarize invoice:
- Item A: $10
Total: 30
```
erica: @zach any chance the chat template removed invisible tokens (zero-width space) or changed preamble that affected prefix alignment? we changed the system->user boundary formatting in rollout.
chris: I reproduced locally with model + tokenizer v2. Small delta in how `'$'` token attaches to numbers — in v1 it was a single token `'$'+'30'`, v2 splits into `'$'` and `30` which could affect postprocessors that rely on token-level joins.
qa-bot: automated regression test failed on invoice_prompt_coverage (diff > 3% F1) — added test case.
zach: possible root cause: we also updated `chat_template` to normalize newlines: `strip_extra_newlines=true` which may collapse the `- Item B: $20` if there's trailing CRLF patterns. I'll run a quick repro with both config flags.
chris: repro steps I used:
```
# shell
python -c "from redwood_tokenizer import Tokenizer; t=Tokenizer('v2'); print(t.encode(' $30'))"
# output: [432, 78]
python -c "print(t.decode([432,78]))"
# output: " 30"
```
maria: customer asks for an ETA and rollback. They are hitting production. They offered logs showing the exact request body (matches above).
erica: we should triage: 1) quick mitigation: revert normalization in hosted for that model or pin to tokenizer v1 for the dedicated pool; 2) longer fix: make postprocessors robust to token splits and avoid collapsing list items on newline normalization.
zach: I can push a hotfix that disables `strip_extra_newlines` for the `invoice_prompt` family in hosted config. @deploy-bot can we schedule a canary rollback for the affected model in region us-west-2?
deploy-bot: scheduled canary rollback: model redwood-open-7b-v2 -> redwood-open-7b-v1 in us-west-2 at 2026-03-10T02:15Z, will run for 15m. :white_check_mark:
chris: also adding a tokenization-aware assertion to our eval suite to detect `$` attachment changes.
maria: communicated rollback plan to customer and asked for samples after rollback.
(30m later)
qa-bot: canary rollback completed, metrics show request-level diffs down to 0.1% for invoice_prompt_coverage. customer confirmed initial sample matches expected output. closing loop?
erica: great. please follow up with postmortem and note the change in tokenizer semantics in release notes.
maria: creating support ticket and pitching a short KB article about tokenizer-sensitive templates.
